transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I’m just so tired. I can barely get through a shift at work lately. It feels like my body is filled with wet sand, and even when I rest, I don’t really feel better.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
I don’t really know. I wouldn’t say I’ve been sad exactly… more just worn out and kind of drained.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?

Yeah… I guess I don’t. Things I usually really like, like cooking, playing guitar, going hiking, even going over to my family’s place, they all just feel kind of flat. Like I’m doing them, but I’m not really into it. It feels like I’m pretending to care.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah. My sleep’s been pretty messed up. With my changing shifts, I got to where I’d only sleep a few hours and still feel kind of wired. And now, even when I’m exhausted, I wake up really early and my mind is already going.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?

Yeah, it’s been kind of all over the place. Lately I just forget to eat, or when I do, food doesn’t really taste like anything… kind of like cardboard. I’ve noticed my work pants are fitting looser too.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Yeah… a lot. I keep feeling like I’ve let everybody down. My manager, my family, even my little nieces. I replay little mistakes from work, like stuff at the register, over and over, and it feels like proof that I’m just… not good enough.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than usual or having trouble sitting still?

Yeah. At first I couldn’t sit still at all—I’d be pacing around the store, straightening things over and over. But lately it’s kind of the opposite. Even walking to the bus feels heavy, and when someone asks me something, it takes me a second to answer, like everything’s slowed down.
Have you felt this way before, or is this the first time you've experienced these feelings and symptoms?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had rough times before, but I don’t know if it was exactly like this. This feels… heavier than what I remember.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About a month, I think. It started around when the store changed our hours for the remodel, and it’s just kind of been going since then.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live or hurting yourself?

Yeah… I have. I’ve had thoughts like maybe everybody would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And a few times walking home, I caught myself thinking about stepping off the curb into traffic. It scares me.
Have your feelings of not wanting to live or hurting yourself included any actual plans or preparations to act on those thoughts?

I haven’t made any real plan or done anything to prepare. It’s more like… I get these scary thoughts, like maybe everyone would be better off if I didn’t wake up. And a few times walking home, I caught myself thinking about stepping off the curb into traffic, but I haven’t set out to do it.
Have these thoughts of not wanting to live or hurting yourself been happening every day?

Not every single day, no… but pretty often. The “not waking up” thought comes up a lot, and a few times when I’m walking home I’ve had that thought about stepping into traffic. It scares me when it happens.
Have these thoughts of not wanting to live or hurting yourself been interfering with your daily life?

Yeah, it has. When those thoughts come up, like not wanting to wake up or thinking about stepping into traffic on the way home, it really shakes me up. I get scared and distracted, and it can make it hard to focus on getting through the day.
Have these thoughts of not wanting to live or hurting yourself been getting worse over the past month?

Yeah… I think they have been a little worse this past month. The “maybe everyone would be better off if I didn’t wake up” thoughts have been coming up more, and those moments walking home where I think about stepping off the curb into traffic have happened a few times. It scares me.
Have you experienced any periods where your depressive symptoms seemed to lift or improve, even if only for a short while, over the past month?

Not really, no. The low, empty feeling has pretty much been there for about four months now. It started after that first rush of energy I had at work passed, and since then I haven’t had much of a break from it.
Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning due to these depressive symptoms?

Yeah, definitely. It’s been affecting work a lot. I’ve started making mistakes at the register, and I’m falling behind on the cash-office stuff. My manager actually took me off some responsibilities I was hoping would help me move up.

And outside of work, I’ve been avoiding my family more. There was even a day I needed same-day crisis help because I didn’t feel safe handling it by myself.
Have you had any days over the past month where you felt somewhat better, or were able to enjoy things or feel a little more energetic?

Not really. I mean, maybe there are moments where I can get through something, but I don’t really enjoy it. Stuff I normally love—cooking, playing guitar, hiking, going over to my family’s—just feels flat. Like I’m doing it because I should, not because I actually care.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your physical movement or activity level over the past month, such as feeling restless or having trouble sitting still?

Yeah. Earlier on I was really restless, like I couldn’t stop pacing around the store or straightening things over and over. But lately it’s kind of the opposite. Even walking to the bus feels heavy, and answering someone takes me longer, like I’m moving through mud.
Have you had any periods over the past two weeks where you felt completely unable to experience any pleasure?

Yeah. Most days it feels like that. Things I usually enjoy—cooking, playing guitar, hiking, even going to my family’s—just feel flat. I can do them sometimes, but it’s like I’m pretending to care, not actually enjoying it.
Have you had any periods over the past month where you felt somewhat better for at least a couple of weeks?

No, not for a couple weeks. The low, empty feeling has pretty much been there about four months now. There was that first rush of energy at work before, but after that passed, I haven’t really had a stretch where I felt better.
